how-tides-work-ab12.title: How tides work
how-tides-work-ab12.hook: Why does the sea rise **twice** a day when the Moon passes overhead only once?
how-tides-work-ab12.oneBreath: The Moon pulls a little harder on the side of Earth facing it than on Earth's centre, and a little less on the far side. That difference stretches the oceans into [[two bulges]], and Earth turns under both of them every day, so most coasts get two high tides.

ideas.title: Gravity weakens with distance
ideas.oneLine: Pull drops quickly as things get farther apart.

ideas.title: A difference in pull stretches Earth
ideas.oneLine: Near side pulled more, far side less: a stretch, not a lift.

ideas.title: Two bulges, not one
ideas.oneLine: The far bulge forms because the far side is pulled less than Earth's centre.

ideas.title: Earth turns under the bulges
ideas.oneLine: Most coasts pass through both bulges each day.

ideas.title: Spring and neap tides
ideas.oneLine: When the Sun lines up with the Moon, the bulges grow.

ideas.title: Why real coastlines differ from the simple picture
ideas.oneLine: Bays, shelves and resonance reshape the tide you actually see.

calibration.q: How many high tides do most coasts get in a day?
calibration.why: Earth turns under two bulges of water, so most places pass through high water twice.

calibration.q: Which has the bigger effect on the tides?
calibration.why: The Sun pulls harder overall, but tides come from the *difference* in pull across Earth, and the nearby Moon wins that by about two to one.

index-funds-cd34.title: How index funds work
index-funds-cd34.hook: How can doing less beat most professional investors?
index-funds-cd34.oneBreath: An index fund buys every company in a market in proportion to its size, so it keeps the market's return minus a tiny fee.

ideas.title: What an index is
ideas.oneLine: A list of companies and a rule for weighting them.

ideas.title: Fees compound too
ideas.oneLine: A 1% fee eats a large share of growth over decades.

ideas.title: Why most active funds lag
ideas.oneLine: Before fees, the average active pound earns the market return.

ideas.title: Diversification
ideas.oneLine: Owning everything removes the risk of any one company.

ideas.title: Staying invested
ideas.oneLine: Missing the best few days costs more than it seems.

minor-keys-ef56.title: Why minor keys sound sad
minor-keys-ef56.hook: Why does lowering one note by a hair change the whole mood of a song?
minor-keys-ef56.oneBreath: A minor chord lowers the middle note of a major chord by one semitone.

ideas.title: Notes are frequencies
ideas.oneLine: Pitch is how fast the air vibrates.

ideas.title: Major and minor thirds
ideas.oneLine: One semitone apart, a world apart in mood.

ideas.title: Culture shapes the feeling
ideas.oneLine: Learned associations matter as much as acoustics.

ideas.title: Hearing it in real songs
ideas.oneLine: The same melody in major and minor.

calibration.q: What changes between a major chord and a minor chord?
calibration.why: Only the middle note, the *third*, drops by one semitone. The other two stay put.

calibration.q: Do people everywhere hear minor keys as sad?
options: Mostly people raised on Western music
calibration.why: The link is strong in Western listeners and weaker elsewhere, so part of it is learned.

notes.claim: Tides are caused by the difference in the Moon's gravitational pull across Earth.

sources.title: Tides and Water Levels
sources.quote: The moon's gravitational pull generates something called the tidal force.

sources.title: Tide | Definition, Causes, Types, & Facts
sources.quote: Tides are caused by the gravitational attraction of the Moon and, to a lesser extent, the Sun.

sources.title: What Causes Tides?
sources.quote: The Moon's gravity pulls on the ocean closest to it, making a bulge.

sources.title: Spring and Neap Tides
sources.quote: Spring tides occur when the sun, moon and Earth are aligned.

say.text: Things pull on each other less when they are further away.
Gravity falls with the square of distance, so doubling the distance leaves a quarter of the pull. That steep drop is why the near side of Earth feels the Moon more than the far side.
The Moon pulls the near ocean more than the middle of Earth, so the water stretches toward it. It is a stretch rather than the whole planet being lifted.

questions.q: Why is there a bulge on the side facing away from the Moon?
Does the Sun make tides too?

say.text: An index is just a list of companies with a rule for how much of each to hold.
